display.purpose: The home hero headline only; one accented phrase inside it. One Display headline per screen at most.

headline.purpose: Every home section head, one size for all (1.5rem, 1.875rem from sm). Card scale, not poster scale.

title-small.purpose: A small story pin's title, clamped to two lines.

body.purpose: Running copy and inputs; 16px is also the touch floor for fields so iOS never zooms. Hero sub-line steps to 1.125rem from sm, max 40ch.

label.purpose: Button text, nav links, See all, trust points.

caption.purpose: Wall caption pills, place and year lines, tab-bar labels.

mono.purpose: Code and the few tabular figures that want a mono: the photo counter pill, the shelf's date line.

shadows.name: elevation-2 (light)
shadows.purpose: Resting; shadow-sm. Story pin photo at rest, header, quiz row, overlay icon buttons.

shadows.name: elevation-3 (light)
shadows.purpose: Raised; shadow-md. Hero search pill, pin photo on hover.

shadows.name: elevation-1 (dark)
shadows.purpose: Dark carries depth in fills; shadows only keep an edge from fusing with the ground.

motion.name: wall-drift
motion.value: translateY 0 to -50%, linear, infinite, 52s / 64s / 58s / 70s / 61s per column, alternating up/down, negative start delays
motion.purpose: The home photo wall. Paused on hover and by the pause button; off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: wall-tile-in
motion.value: 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), from opacity 0 translateY(18px) scale(0.97), stagger 120ms + 55ms per tile
motion.purpose: The one tile entrance on first paint; fill backwards so content is visible if it never runs.

motion.name: focus-ring
motion.value: outline 3px solid var(--accent), offset 3px; offset transitions 140ms

motion.name: vt-ease
motion.purpose: Route transitions (320ms slides / crossfade), tab-bar pill (250ms), tab-bar hide (280ms).

motion.name: photo-hover-zoom
motion.value: scale(1.03) pin, 1.04 wall tile, 1.04 place tile; 300-500ms ease-out inside the clip

components.description: Filter and form field: 44px, 10px radius, hairline, surface fill, label above.

narrative.overview:
Kakinotes looks like the photo apps its readers already live in: the stories' own photos lead, set as soft rounded tiles on a calm, warm ground, with the words sitting quietly underneath. It is the category's standard app language (the owner's pinned reference is Instagram / Pinterest), chosen deliberately, so nothing about the frame competes with the places and people in the pictures. Real photos from real accounts are the only imagery; there is no illustration, no texture, no themed costume.

Comfort for long reading in both themes is the material premise. Light is a soft warm gray, never stark white; dark is a soft warm charcoal, never pure black, with off-white ink to cut glare. Both renditions share one warm hue family and one blue accent that only ever marks something the reader can act on. Density is app-like: section heads at card scale rather than poster scale, story pins two to four across, controls as pills, and one living element on the home screen (a slowly drifting wall of story photos) rather than many small announcements.

The previous "Night Field" world (near-black slate ground, cyan accent, the dotted night-sky hero, always-dark photographic bands) is retired and its hero has been deleted. Do not bring any of it back, and do not swap in another costume world; film prints and crate labels were turned down for the same reason.

This is stage 1 of an app-wide redesign. The home screen, the story pins, the place tiles, the footer and the filter bar have had the dedicated pass. Story pages, My Stories, the editor and the staff tools inherit the tokens below automatically but have not been redesigned yet; where this file says nothing specific about them, it is because no rule has been decided, not because the old one still holds.
keyCharacteristics: Story photos lead; every photo is rounded on its own and nothing boxes it in.
Warm-gray ground in light, warm charcoal in dark; one warm hue family across both.
One blue accent, used only for actions, focus, active states and the headline's accent word.
Figtree throughout; hierarchy by weight and tracking, not by a second face.
Pills for controls, rounded-2xl for photos (story pins and place tiles alike).
Shadows carry depth in light; surface fills carry it in dark.
One slow, pausable drift on the home hero; otherwise motion is feedback, not decoration.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: The accent marks actions, focus, active states and the headline's accent words, and nothing decorative. No second brand colour. Semantic status colours in the staff moderation tools and the two staff/editor data palettes above are the only exceptions, because they carry meaning rather than brand.

rules.name: The Warm Ground Rule
rules.body: Neither rendition ever uses stark white or pure black as a ground. Any new neutral is a member of the same warm family (hue around 70-85 in OKLCH, very low chroma); a cool gray or slate next to these reads as a leftover.

rules.name: The Two Renditions Rule
rules.body: Every colour is decided for both themes at once, as a token with two values in the four token blocks of `app/globals.css`, never as a one-off `dark:` override.

rules.name: The One Switch Rule
rules.body: `data-theme="light"|"dark"` on `<html>` is the only theming signal. A blocking script in `app/layout.tsx` sets it before paint, the theme toggle flips it, and the `@custom-variant dark` declaration binds Tailwind's `dark:` to the same attribute. Never remove that declaration or add a second signal.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Figtree everywhere, including headings. There is no serif and no second display face; hierarchy comes from weight and tracking.

rules.name: The Card-Scale Heading Rule
rules.body: Section heads stay at Headline size, never display size: this is an app screen, not a poster. Display is reserved for one headline per screen.

rules.name: The Edge-Bleed Rule
rules.body: A sideways row on a phone runs to the screen edges (negative margin, inner padding) so the cut-off item at the edge is the swipe affordance; it wraps or sits in the container from `sm` up. The place tiles do this. No "swipe" hint text.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: Tailwind's whole `shadow-*` scale is rebound to the themed elevation tokens, so every shadow is correct in both renditions. Never write an arbitrary `shadow-[...]` value; it can only be tuned for one ground. The tiny dark halo under photo dots is the one sanctioned exception, because it sits on a photo, not on the ground.

rules.name: The Recess Rule
rules.body: The recess colour is for things set into the page (a photo's loading ground, an input, a switch thumb), never for grouping content into a panel.

rules.name: The Rounded Photo Rule
rules.body: A story photo carries its own rounded corners and is never placed inside a bordered or filled box to get them.

rules.name: The Pill Control Rule
rules.body: A new interactive control at button or chip scale is a pill. (The filter bar's desktop Apply / Reset buttons and form fields still use the 10px step; they predate this pass and are not a pattern to copy for buttons.)

rules.name: The Boxless Pin Rule
rules.body: A story card has no border and no background box. The photo carries the shape; the words share the page.

rules.name: The Place-Is-Not-A-Story Rule
rules.body: A place is shown as a small rounded photo tile with its name underneath, never as a round, ringed photo in a row: that shape is Instagram's "story" row, and a place is not a story (owner decision 2026-11-17).
rules.section: A place is shown as a small rounded photo tile with its name underneath, never as a round, ringed photo in a row: that shape is Instagram's "story" row, and a place is not a story (owner decision 2026-11-17).

rules.name: The Pausable Motion Rule
rules.body: Anything that moves on its own for more than five seconds holds still on hover, ships a visible pause control, and does not start at all under reduced motion. Animate transform and opacity only.

dos: Do let real story photos lead every browsing surface; rounded at 16px, clipped, on the ground.
Do keep the blue accent for actions, focus, active states and the headline's accent words only (The One Blue Rule).
Do decide every new colour for both renditions as a two-value token (The Two Renditions Rule).
Do make new controls at button or chip scale full pills with at least a 44px tap area.
Do use the `shadow-*` scale (rebound to the elevation tokens) for depth in light and surface steps for depth in dark.
Do add the `press` utility to anything tappable, and `press-hover-only` on large scroll-through surfaces.
Do give anything that moves for more than five seconds a pause control, a hover hold and a reduced-motion off state (The Pausable Motion Rule).
Do keep section heads at Headline size; one Display headline per screen at most.
donts: Don't bring back any part of Night Field: the near-black slate ground, the cyan accent, the dotted hero, or always-dark bands that ignore the theme.
Don't use stark white or pure black as a ground, or a cool gray beside the warm neutrals (The Warm Ground Rule).
Don't put a border or a filled box around a story card (The Boxless Pin Rule).
Don't show places as round, ringed photos in a row (The Place-Is-Not-A-Story Rule).
Don't add a second accent, a serif, or a second display face.
Don't write an arbitrary `shadow-[...]` value on the page ground (The One Ramp Rule).
Don't use the recess colour as a grouping panel (The Recess Rule).
Don't add star ratings, review scores, "Book Now"/"Explore Now" CTAs, traveller-count badges or avatar-stack social proof (PRODUCT.md anti-patterns).
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons; icons are drawn SVG from `components/icons.tsx`.
Don't invent new rules for story pages, My Stories or the editor from this file; they have not had their redesign pass yet.
